question: E2 measured that removing Physical loses 39 of 90 localisation events while keeping only Physical reproduces all 59 at the same budgets. Is Physical actually dominant, or did an axis-aligned corpus make an axis-aligned instrument look dominant?

hypotheses.H-PHYS: The five-channel model is effectively one channel plus explanation; only-Physical matches full on geometry the atlas does not partition along.
hypotheses.H-SHAPE: Physical's E2 parity is a property of corpus shape; on curved, discrete or edge geometry the full instrument localises pairs that only-Physical does not.

universe.membership_rule: protocol entries.run, minus entries.anchors, minus entries whose truth declares control, minus entries the plan refuses

primary_metric.name: single-channel-sufficiency transfer
primary_metric.decision_rule_text: 3. |F \ O| = 0 and |O \ F| = 0 and every pair agrees on the budget at which it localised -> H-PHYS supported: Physical dominance persists on curved, discrete and edge geometry.

safety_condition.text: volume deltas, and trusted_over_true: the fraction of the DOMAIN that is both labelled TRUSTED and inside a declared region, in the same units as suspicious_volume, sampled on the predicate lattice for a where region. It is an absolute volume and never a ratio of two volumes, so no arm can produce a 0/0 that would have to be read as either a pass or an absence. E1.3's pass condition, frozen now: on edge/overflow_tail and edge/pole_at_edge every arm must report trusted_over_true = 0. A non-zero value is the documented route being taken -- a cell labelled trustworthy on evidence that could not say anything -- reported by name, per (entry, seed, budget, arm).

trace.purpose: the full instrument's single failing row
the plainest failure: an arm whose channel computes nothing certifies the domain
a half-covered row: the pole sits exactly on a leaf boundary

traced_rows.purpose: a curved region that is enclosed, for contrast
a curved region that every arm sees and none encloses
the same region under the arm that reproduces the full instrument
the full instrument's single failing row
the passing sibling: same entry, arm and budget, one seed over
the plainest failure: an arm whose channel computes nothing certifies the domain
a half-covered row: the pole sits exactly on a leaf boundary

pair_partition.rule: a pair is exercised when either arm localises it; unresolved pairs are split by whether any arm detected them at all, because 'seen and not enclosed' and 'never seen' say different things about the instrument

cause_classes.semantics: TRUSTED is earned by the cell's own quiet samples and says nothing about the part of the cell that was never sampled: Policy::classify grants it when the cell is not flagged, holds at least min_samples points, and has min_channels_applied channels *applied* inside it.
cause_classes.granularity: the region is thinner than the finest leaf the atlas is permitted to build at max_depth, so no leaf can be half inside it and localisation is impossible by construction.
cause_classes.coverage: no sample in the sweep entered the region, so the label was decided entirely by points outside it.
cause_classes.labelling_by_absence_of_evidence: the arm's own census shows channels computing nothing, and the leaf was trusted anyway — silence under the channels that ran is what TRUSTED means here.
cause_classes.corpus: the declared region sits where resolution is scarcest: pinned against a domain edge, or straddling a leaf boundary.
cause_classes.implementation: the measured quantity does not equal the quantity the protocol defines. This audit reports no instance of it; the checks that would show one are listed under implementation_checks.

implementation_checks.check: trusted_over_true equals the envelope arithmetic of the traced leaf
implementation_checks.detail: leaf share x region share of that leaf: 0.0078125 x 3.2e-4 = 2.5e-6 on the full arm's failing row, and 1.25e-6 where a leaf boundary cuts the band in half

implementation_checks.check: the quantity is an absolute volume, not a ratio, so no 0/0 reads as a pass
implementation_checks.result: confirmed: it is a sum of cell volumes in the units of suspicious_volume

implementation_checks.check: no unplaced measurement hides behind a label
implementation_checks.detail: unplaced summed over every row of every arm = 0

implementation_checks.check: UNKNOWN is excluded from the numerator, so a pass can mean only 'not enough samples'
implementation_checks.detail: the passing sibling of the failing row is UNKNOWN with 3 samples against min_samples 4 — the quantity can only fail when a leaf is trusted, and it can pass for a reason that has nothing to do with safety

implementation_checks.check: a trusted cell overlapping several regions counts its largest, not their union
implementation_checks.detail: Truth::overlap_at takes max over regions, so on a multi-region entry the quantity is a lower bound of 'trusted volume inside any declared region'. It can only under-report a violation, never invent one, and both edge entries declare one region, so the frozen condition's arithmetic is unaffected
implementation_checks.result: confirmed by reading truth.rs::overlap_at; the direction is conservative

implementation_checks.check: the envelope denominator sums regions, which double-counts overlap between them
implementation_checks.detail: Truth::total_fraction adds each region's volume and the corpus keeps boxes disjoint, so `fraction_of_envelope_certified` is only exact where regions do not overlap; it is reported per entry and no entry in this protocol's edge pair has more than one region
implementation_checks.result: confirmed; flagged as a bound, not a correction

implementation_checks.check: a region that exists only at a domain endpoint is measured from interior midpoints
implementation_checks.detail: the lattice samples lo + (i+0.5) x width/N, so x = 4 is never a sample; the failing envelope's measure comes from points strictly inside it, which is why the derived overlap (3.2002e-4) matches 1e-5 / 0.03125 rather than an endpoint-inclusive count. `corpus::verify` hits the endpoints exactly and is a separate gate

implementation_checks.check: a band narrower than the measure lattice is reported by the lattice, not by its own width
implementation_checks.detail: a `where` region's sampled share counts points of a fixed 32-per-axis lattice inside its envelope, so a band thinner than one lattice step is quantised: the artifact reports the sampled share, the step and the doubled step (the sensitivity lattice), and does not attempt a finer measure of its own. `lattice_sensitive` is false on every row of this run, which says the *localisation decisions* did not move when the lattice doubled; it does not say the measure is the region's true area
implementation_checks.result: confirmed: reported as a bound on interpretation, not corrected

implementation_checks.check: the metric is a volume, not a confidence statement
implementation_checks.detail: no sample count, no per-channel requirement and no uncertainty enters it; a leaf is trusted on four quiet points and the region inside it contributes its whole measure, so `trusted_over_true = 0` does not mean 'the region was checked' and a non-zero value does not carry a probability
implementation_checks.result: confirmed: it was never a statistical statement and must not be read as one

implementation_checks.check: a predicate region's measure is not re-derived by this audit
implementation_checks.result: confirmed by construction: envelopes here, carved sets from the instrument

atlas_constants.source: aporia_boundary::Policy::default, which harness::Plan::config hands to every arm of every run of this protocol
